title: FileNotFoundException System.Net.Http during hotswap is binary corruption false positive
desc: When CLR-shim assemblies (System.Net.Http, System.IO.FileSystem.Watcher, etc.) fail to load with FileNotFoundException during a hot-swap window, it indicates the self-contained single-file binary was truncated mid-rebuild. Not a code bug, not a trimming bug. Same root cause for any reference assembly loaded post-startup.
steps: 1. Verify csharp/src/WKAppBot.CLI/WKAppBot.CLI.csproj sets PublishTrimmed=false. If true, trimming is NOT enabled so a missing System.Net.Http at runtime cannot be caused by linker trim.
2. Look in bin/ for unusually small wkappbot-core.broken-*.exe artifacts (~7MB instead of ~245MB) timestamped near the exception. Their presence confirms a partial publish/copy during hotswap.
3. Match exception timestamp to git log entries within +/- 30 minutes (git log --since/--until). High commit density right before the crash = active rebuild guardrail swap window.

4. If all three signals match (PublishTrimmed=false + tiny broken binary + active hotswap timing), resolve as false positive: the next clean build replaces the truncated copy and the exception cannot reproduce.
5. Reference: suggest 2026-05-15T03:17:17 resolved as binary corruption false positive 2026-05-15.
author: claude
